(C.I.D.) Office Notes
Foreign Section, C.I.D.
January 29, 1929.

Inquiries go to show that Kang Chang Ze(姜昌濟)
who resides in the French Concession boarded the train
which was due to leave Shanghai North Station for Nanking
at 11 p.m. on January 25 and while seated inside was
accosted by a Chinese who inquired if he was Mr. Kang.
On his answering in the affirmative the Chinese requested
Kang to meet a Japanese friend who was waiting on the
platform. Kang complied with the request and was
immediately taken into custody by Japanese Consular
Policeman Yokoda on a charge of murder and robbery.
Kang complained that he was a naturalised Chinese and
called one of the railway police to whom he explained
matters. Both Kang and the Japanese Consular Policeman
were then escorted to the Paoshan Road Police Station,
Chapei where the latter officer demanded that Kang be
handed over on the charges for which he had been arrested.
The Chinese authorities refused to hand Kang over and the
Japanese consequently left. Kang was detained over
night in the Paoshan Road Station and released on January
26. It is reported that Kang Chang Ze(姜昌濟) is a
naturalised Chinese citizen and until his arrest was
employed as a detective attached to the Third Section
of the Civil Department of the Kiangsu Provincial
Government.

H. S. Kim.

A/ D. C. I.

Mr. 29/1

(刑事侦缉处) 办公室笔记
刑事侦缉处外籍科
1929年1月29日。

经查询显示，居住在法租界的姜昌济（Kang Chang Ze）于1月25日晚11点登上了原定从上海北站开往南京的火车，当他在车内就座时，一名中国人上前搭讪，询问他是否是姜先生。在他给予肯定答复后，该中国人请求姜去见一位在站台上等候的日本朋友。姜应允了该请求，随即被日本领事馆警察横田（Yokoda）以谋杀和抢劫罪名拘留。姜投诉称自己是归化中国公民，并叫来一名铁路警察向其说明情况。随后，姜和日本领事馆警察均被护送至闸北宝山路巡捕房，后者要求中方移交因上述罪名被捕的姜。中方当局拒绝移交姜，日本人遂离开。姜在宝山路巡捕房被羁押过夜，并于1月26日获释。据报道，姜昌济（Kang Chang Ze）是一名归化中国公民，在被捕前受雇于江苏省政府民政厅第三科，担任侦探。

H. S. Kim.

代理副督察长

先生 29/1

January 26, 1929, Morning Translation.
....................
MISCELLANEOUS NOTORIOUS KOREAN DESPERADO ARRESTED AT NORTH STATION
BY RAILWAY GUARDS AT THE REQUEST OF JAPANESE POLICE

The Shanghai Nichi Nichi and the Shanghai Mainichi
publish the following report:-
On the night of January 25 a squad of detectives attached
to the local Japanese Consulate went to the Shanghai North
Station in the hope of arresting a notorious Korean named
Tsiang Hwa Tsao(姜華祖), alias Tsiang Chong Che(姜昌濟),
alias Tsiang Tung Yoh(姜東郁) who is wanted by the Japanese
authorities for the murder of another Korean on Hannen Road
some time last year and also for several other murders per-
petrated in the French Concession as well as for several
robberies.
Tsiang, who had apparently been forewarned, cleverly
eluded the Police cordon and managed to enter the station
compound where he hurriedly bought a ticket and boarded a
train bound for Nanking. The Japanese Police thereupon lost
no time in getting into touch with one of the responsible
railway officials who kindly instructed the railway guards
to remove Tsiang from the train.
Tsiang is now in the custody of Chinese Police who are
reluctant to hand over the prisoner to the Japanese authorities
despite their repeated representations.
Local Chinese newspapers published this news yesterday,
but they were greatly exaggerated.
Recently Tsiang graduated from a Chinese Detective
School and has ever since been posing as a Chinese, claiming
to have been naturalized as such.
Besides being one of the leaders of the so-called Ping
Ying Volunteer Corps, a radical organ of recalcitrant
Koreans, Tsiang is also said to be responsible for the two
bomb incidents at the local Japanese Consulate in April and
September 1928. Many of his accomplices in numerous cases
of murder and robbery are either serving terms of imprison-
ment or are under trial.
............................
-do- ARRIVAL OF NEW JAPANESE CONSULAR OFFICIALS

The Shanghai Nichi Nichi, Shanghai Nippo and the Shanghai
Mainichi publish the following report:-
Vice-Consul M. Tanaka, formerly attached to the Japanese
Consulate-General at Hankow, arrived here yesterday from
Japan to take over the position in the Japanese Consulate-
General here in succession to Consul Shimizu.
Mr. K. Okazaki, Vice-Consul, and Mr. T. Nomura, a
Secretary in the Japanese Legation in Peking, also arrived
here on January 25 aboard the s. s. Sakaki Maru to take over
their new posts in the local Consulate.
Vice-Consul Okazaki is a well-known middle-distance
runner having taken part in the last Olympic Games.

1929年1月26日，上午译文。
....................
应日本警方要求，铁路警卫在北站逮捕一名朝鲜籍著名亡命之徒

《上海日日新闻》和《上海每日新闻》刊登如下报道：-
1月25日晚，隶属于当地日本领事馆的一队侦探前往上海北站，希望能逮捕一名名为姜华祖（Tsiang Hwa Tsao），又名姜昌济（Tsiang Chong Che），又名姜东郁（Tsiang Tung Yoh）的朝鲜籍著名亡命之徒，日本当局因其在去年于汉密路（Hannen Road）谋杀另一名朝鲜人，以及在法租界犯下的数起其他谋杀案和多起抢劫案而通缉此人。
姜显然已事先得到警告，巧妙地避开了警察的包围圈，并设法进入车站区域，匆忙购票后登上了一列开往南京的火车。日本警方随即不失时机地联系了一位负责的铁路官员，该官员好意指示铁路警卫将姜从火车上带离。
姜目前由中国警方羁押，尽管日方多次交涉，中方仍不愿将该囚犯移交给日本当局。
当地中文报纸昨日刊登了这一消息，但内容多有夸大。
姜最近从中国侦探学校毕业，此后一直伪装成中国人，声称已归化为中国公民。
除了是所谓“平英义勇队”（一个顽固朝鲜人的激进组织）的领导人之一外，据说姜还应对1928年4月和9月发生在当地日本领事馆的两起炸弹事件负责。他在多起谋杀和抢劫案中的许多同伙要么正在服刑，要么正在受审。
............................
-同上- 新任日本领事官员抵沪

《上海日日新闻》、《上海新报》和《上海每日新闻》刊登如下报道：-
前驻汉口日本总领事馆副领事田中（M. Tanaka）先生昨日从日本抵达此处，接替清水（Shimizu）领事出任本地日本总领事馆职务。
副领事冈崎（K. Okazaki）先生和北京日本公使馆秘书野村 T.（T. Nomura）先生也于1月25日乘坐“榊丸”号（s. s. Sakaki Maru）轮抵达此处，就任本地领事馆的新职。
副领事冈崎是一位著名的中长跑运动员，曾参加上一届奥林匹克运动会。

pages.en:
THE EVENING NEWS, MONDAY, JANUARY 28, 19

Korean Charged
With 5 Murders
Arrested After
Nine-Year
Manhunt Of
International
Mystery, Now
A Prisoner

A nine-year man-hunt for a
Japanese assassin ended
Saturday afternoon with the arrest
of the Shanghai Mystery Man,
otherwise known as a Korean
resident of this city, who has been
wanted in connection with five
murders and other crimes dating
back to 1932. A head of the list is
the murder of General Shirakawa,
commander of the Japanese forces
in China. The arrest was made by
Shanghai police and two constables
of the Japanese Army, just as he
was boarding a boat for Nanking.
The Japanese had a permit from
the Chinese authorities to make the
arrest in Chinese territory. It was
stated that he had been "kidnapped"
a Chinese. Japanese consular
investigations have failed to
substantiate his claims but he is
being held by the Chinese officials
pending proof of Japanese authority.

He has been wanted on a Japanese
extradition warrant since April
1932 for alleged murder of a
Japanese who was shot on January
29th in the Hongkew district. The
murder is alleged to have been the
sequel to a quarrel between the
Koreans regarding anti-Japanese
activities. He is also accused of the
wholesale assassination of four
Koreans, who were implicated in
the French Concession. The chief
charge against him is that he
masterminded the assassination of
General Shirakawa, commander of
the Japanese forces in China, on
April 29, 1932.
pages.zh:
《晚邮报》，星期一，1月28日，19

朝鲜人被控
犯下5起谋杀案
在经过九年
国际谜团般的
追捕后被捕，
现为囚犯

对一名日本刺客长达九年的追捕于周六下午结束，这名被称为“上海神秘人”的男子被捕，他是本市的一名朝鲜居民，因涉及五起谋杀案及其他可追溯至1932年的罪行而被通缉。通缉名单之首的是谋杀日军驻华司令白川义则将军一案。逮捕行动由上海警察和两名日本陆军宪兵执行，当时他正登船前往南京。日方持有中国当局颁发的许可证，得以在中国领土实施逮捕。据称他“绑架”了一名中国人。日本领事馆的调查未能证实他的说法，但在日方权限得到证明之前，他正由中国官员羁押。

自1932年4月以来，他一直持有一张日本引渡令，被指控谋杀了一名于1月29日在虹口地区被枪杀的日本人。据称该谋杀案是朝鲜人之间因反日活动发生争吵后的结果。他还被指控大规模暗杀四名卷入法租界事件的朝鲜人。针对他的主要指控是，他策划了1932年4月29日对日军驻华司令白川义则将军的暗杀。
